result.instructions: Tools for Lightspeed Retail (X-Series), hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "What were my total sales yesterday, by outlet and payment type?"; "Which products are below their reorder point at my main outlet?"; "Show the supplier stock orders that have not arrived yet.". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes Lightspeed Retail (X-Series) data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run lightspeedxseries_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run lightspeedxseries_request_feature to record the request. Paid plan: Pro (unlimited tool calls (fair use limit: 10,000 a month), $9/month or $90/year). Pro can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run lightspeedxseries_upgrade (plan "monthly" or "yearly"); it returns a payment link for the user to open. lightspeedxseries_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_list_products
tools.title: List products
tools.description: List products (variants) in the catalog: id, family_id, sku, variant_name, prices (price_excluding_tax / price_including_tax), active flags, codes, suppliers, version. The product NAME lives on the product family: add includes=["families"] to get it. Paginate with next_after (stop when data is empty). With sku set, only that SKU is looked up and the other filters are ignored. For text/brand/supplier filters use search_products; for stock use get_inventory_levels. GET /products.

sku.description: Exact SKU (other filters are ignored when set).

includes.description: Related records to include. 'families' is required together with brands, categories, suppliers, tags, variant_attributes or customizations.

sku.description: SKU filter (sent in lowercase, as the vendor search requires).

variant_parent_id.description: Only the variants of this parent product.

deleted.description: true = include deleted records (default: active only).

offset.description: Offset for the next page: pass next_offset from the previous call (default 0).

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_get_inventory_levels
tools.title: Get inventory levels
tools.description: Stock on hand per product per outlet: product_id, location_id (= outlet id), current_inventory_level, reorder threshold/amount, quantity_to_procure, average cost, total cost, supplier. Filter by outlet_ids, product_ids (or root_product_ids for variant families), supplier_ids; to_be_procured_only keeps products with a positive quantity_to_procure (the vendor's re-order suggestion, which accounts for open orders); for a plain below-reorder-point list, compare current_inventory_level with reorder_threshold yourself. Offset paging: pass next_offset to continue (null = last page). Read-only even though the vendor takes the filter as a POST body. POST /inventory_levels.

outlet_ids.description: Only these outlets (the vendor calls them location_ids).

product_ids.description: Only these products. Not together with root_product_ids.

root_product_ids.description: Only these variant families (use with group_variants). Not together with product_ids.

to_be_procured_only.description: true = only products with a positive quantity_to_procure (not the same as below the reorder point).

group_variants.description: Aggregate variant families when filtering by root_product_ids.

offset.description: Offset for the next page: pass next_offset from the previous call (default 0).

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_search_sales
tools.title: Search sales
tools.description: Find sales by date range (UTC), state, outlet, register, user, customer, payment type, product or invoice number. Uses offset paging: pass next_offset to continue (null = last page). Replies can be large: for totals over a period use sales_summary instead of paging through this. GET /search?type=sales.

date_from.description: Sales from this UTC time. YYYY-MM-DD means the start of that UTC day; or 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z. Convert local days to UTC with the retailer's time zone.

date_to.description: Sales up to this UTC time. YYYY-MM-DD means the END of that UTC day (23:59:59Z).

state.description: Sale state. On-account and layby sales are state closed (they differ by attributes).

user_id.description: Only sales by this staff user.

payment_type_id.description: Only sales with this payment type (the payment type's config_id, shown as payments[].type.config_id in a sale).

offset.description: Offset for the next page: pass next_offset from the previous call (default 0).

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_sales_summary
tools.title: Sales summary (totals for a period)
tools.description: Totals for a period computed here from up to max_pages x page_size sales, so a report needs ONE tool call instead of dozens: sale count and net / tax / gross (tax-inclusive) totals, plus breakdowns by state, UTC day, outlet and payment type name, and the top products by quantity. By default only closed sales are counted (states containing 'closed'); set counted_states to change that. Dates are UTC (convert local days with the retailer's time zone). If the reply says truncated, call again with offset = next_offset and add the figures up. Uses GET /search?type=sales.

date_from.description: Sales from this UTC time. YYYY-MM-DD means the start of that UTC day; or 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z. Convert local days to UTC with the retailer's time zone.

date_to.description: Sales up to this UTC time. YYYY-MM-DD means the END of that UTC day (23:59:59Z).

state.description: Sale state. On-account and layby sales are state closed (they differ by attributes).

user_id.description: Only sales by this staff user.

payment_type_id.description: Only sales with this payment type (the payment type's config_id, shown as payments[].type.config_id in a sale).

counted_states.description: Sale states that count towards the totals (exact, case-insensitive). Default: every state containing 'closed'.

max_pages.description: Pages of page_size sales to read (default 5, max 20).

offset.description: Offset for the next page: pass next_offset from the previous call (default 0).

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_create_customer
tools.title: Create customer
tools.description: WRITE: create a new customer. Give at least a first name, last name or company name. Check search_customers first so you do not create a duplicate. POST /customers.

customer_code.description: Unique customer code (generated when omitted on create).

physical_country_id.description: Country code such as US, CA, AU.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_update_customer
tools.title: Update customer
tools.description: WRITE: change fields of an existing customer. Only the fields you pass change: the tool first reads the customer and sends the vendor its full record with your changes applied (the vendor's update is a full PUT). Cannot delete a customer or change balances. Lightspeed offers no partial update for customers, so a change made by someone else in the moments between the tool's read and its write can be overwritten. PUT /customers/{customer_id}.

customer_code.description: Unique customer code (generated when omitted on create).

physical_country_id.description: Country code such as US, CA, AU.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_update_product_prices
tools.title: Update product prices
tools.description: WRITE: set the selling price of one product (variant). Pass price_excluding_tax or price_including_tax as a decimal string such as "24.99" (set one; the store's tax setting decides which the till uses). Nothing else on the product changes. Read the product first and confirm the new price with the user. PATCH /products/{product_id}.

tools.name: lightspeedxseries_set_product_stock
tools.title: Set product stock and reorder levels
tools.description: WRITE: set the stock on hand (current_amount) and/or the reorder point and reorder amount of ONE product at ONE outlet. current_amount is the NEW TOTAL on hand, not a change: it overwrites the count, so sales made since you last read it are lost from the count. Read get_inventory_levels first and confirm the number with the user. Other outlets and all other product fields stay as they are. PATCH /products/{product_id} (outlet_inventories).

current_amount.description: New stock on hand at this outlet (the total, not a delta).

reorder_point.description: Re-order when stock falls to this level.

annotations.title: Set product stock and reorder levels
